---
title: "Tiny DSA"
---

Tiny DSA is a small Python reimplementation of an Excel workbook for exploring
general-government debt-to-GDP dynamics over a five-year horizon. It is aimed
at economists who want a transparent, hand-traceable baseline and one
configurable stress scenario.

::: {.callout-warning}
Tiny DSA is a methodological artifact, not an operational debt-sustainability
framework. It is not validated against country data and is not endorsed by the
IMF, the World Bank, or any other institution. Do not use its results for
policy decisions without a substantially richer model and independent review.
:::

## Start here

1. [Install the package and learn the API](user-guide/functional-overview.qmd).
2. [Run a complete Borvelia example](user-guide/illustrative-example.qmd).
3. [Review the debt identity and modeling limits](user-guide/methodology.qmd).
4. [Read the Excel parity evidence](user-guide/excel-parity-validation.qmd).

The public import path is `tiny_dsa.api`. The three public functions return
the baseline path, the shocked path, or their difference in percentage points:
`compute_output_baseline`, `compute_output_shocked`, and
`compute_output_delta`.

## Install

Run this command in a shell:

`uv add "tiny-dsa @ git+https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-tiny-dsa"`

The tool uses real GDP growth, real interest rates, and primary balances
expressed as percentages. It omits inflation, exchange-rate effects,
stock-flow adjustments, endogenous fiscal responses, and debt thresholds.
